full_normalized_abstract: For the fixed birational map L(u,v)=(u,(u^2+1)v), reduction at every prime p≡3(mod 4) permutes all of F_p^2. Its point-weighted distribution of periods divided by p has no limit. At every fixed 1/2≤ x<1, the distribution function is 1-φ(p-1)/(p-1)+o(1), with limsup 1 and liminf at most 23/24. Moreover, neither these distribution-function values nor the period measures converge on any further prime subset of positive upper relative density. The latter statement uses the classical continuous empirical law for φ(p-1)/(p-1). A supplementary proposition treats all odd primes on the invariant regular domain, and under uniform-point deletion or arbitrary exceptional-period completion. These conventions cannot restore convergence on any positive-upper-density prime selection. The contribution is a precisely delimited application to the broad existence assertion in the 2004 Oberwolfach problem on finite-field maps. The triangular family, primitive-value estimates, totient mean and scalar distribution law are established ingredients; no new arithmetic theorem or historical firstness is claimed.
